findings.text: §26's done-when runs `crew repair --review --set status=superseded` and requires "the record reads superseded afterwards", but `repair_run_review` refuses any `status=` value outside `RECOGNISED_REVIEW_STATUSES` (`reckon/crew/review.py:3317-3322`), and that set is `{parsed, unparsed, incomplete}` (`reckon/crew/review.py:904-906`); `superseded` is not a stored review status — `reckon/crew/review_lifecycle.py` derives it and writes nothing. Relaxing only the directory check, as the deliverable states, leaves the first case still refused on the status, and the repaired body would also fail `review_record_refusals`, so the case cannot pass on the declared change and the same value would change what every reader treats as a review status

findings.text: §25's two cases are asserted as "not refused by `_unreviewed_refusal`" and "is refused", but `_unreviewed_refusal` is a message builder that always returns a string (`reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1406`); the refusal is the caller's `raise CrewError(_unreviewed_refusal(...))` around line 1207, so the named instrument produces identical output on the refusing and the accepting path and cannot distinguish the two cases
